data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add or extend review-stats.sh to emit p90_cycle_count, phantom_escalation_rate, call2_finding_drop_rate, prior_region_resustain_skew over rolling 7-day and 30-day windows. Document response playbook: when phantom_escalation_rate exceeds threshold for two consecutive 7-day windows, open a P2 bug against the cycle-1 severity rubric. Same playbook for prior_region_resustain_skew anomalies (P2 bug against the two-call architecture / prior_findings_index design). Threshold values themselves deferred to first 30-day data.
**Why**: SC6 forward telemetry. Provides leading indicators of severity-inflation drift and prior-salience suppression so the team can intervene early.
**Scope**:
  IN:
  - review-stats.sh emits the four named metrics in 7-day and 30-day windows
  - Response playbook documented in plugins/dso/docs/review-telemetry-playbook.md (or equivalent)
  - Alert owner identified (review-pipeline maintainer)
  OUT:
  - DefenseStore + severity_history (S7)
  - Arbiter (S10)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, review-stats.sh reports the four named metrics and the response playbook is documented
  ← Satisfies: "Migration via best-effort file-path binding, fixture-based validation, and forward telemetry"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Threshold tuning deferred to first 30-day data — metrics need a baseline before alerts are meaningful

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a project maintainer, review-stats.sh reports four named telemetry metrics with a documented response playbook
